Implement the CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive live context for the Cleaner CRM Phoenix app at /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm.

FIRST: call the mcp start_task tool with requirement_name="implementation_file", entity_type="component", entity_id="962dbf7f-fd66-52e0-be22-fffc20461748" (pass your registered agent_id if supported). Its response is the authoritative work prompt — follow it (spec file, rules, templates). If start_task errors, tell me in your final response and proceed from the component spec at .code_my_spec/spec/cleaner_crm_web/ (find the ClientLive spec) plus the guidance below.

Context you need:
- ADRs in .code_my_spec/architecture/decisions/ (LiveView, DaisyUI, audit-logging, money-handling). Rules in .code_my_spec/rules/ (liveview_design.md, live_context_design.md, liveview_forms.md).
- The BDD specs in test/spex/832_manage_clients_and_properties_with_access_details/ are the acceptance contract — read them ALL first; they define routes (~p"/clients", ~p"/clients/new", ~p"/clients/:id", ~p"/clients/:id/properties/new"), form selectors ([data-test='client-form'], [data-test='property-form']...), and behaviors (access details day-of visibility, deactivation with upcoming jobs, audit logging of entry-code changes).
- This will need the CleanerCrm.Clients context (Client, Property, AccessDetail schemas + migrations) and likely stubs of CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder — check .code_my_spec/spec/cleaner_crm/clients* specs and implement the context + schemas + migration as needed to make ClientLive work. Scope everything by the current account (CleanerCrm.Users.Scope carries active_account after picker; require an account).
- Routes go in the :require_authenticated_user live_session in lib/cleaner_crm_web/router.ex.
- Match existing code style (see lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/account_live/* as the house style; DaisyUI classes; CoreComponents).

Verify: mix compile clean (no errors), mix format, then run the story's specs: `mix spex test/spex/832_manage_clients_and_properties_with_access_details/` — make as many green as the Clients domain allows (criteria touching jobs/audit UIs may stay red until Scheduling/Audit land; get the client/property CRUD + access-detail criteria green). Run `mix test` to ensure no regressions.

Final response: what you implemented (files), spec pass/fail counts for the 832 directory, and anything blocked on other contexts. Under 200 words.
</teammate-message>

  @moduledoc """
  Story 832 — Manage clients and properties with access details
  Criterion 7107 — Adding a property under an existing client saves it
  and lists it under that client as its only owning client.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story832.Criterion7113Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 832 — Manage clients and properties with access details
  Criterion 7113 — Updating a property's lockbox code propagates to
  the brief of its already-scheduled future jobs.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "updated entry code propagates to future jobs" do
    scenario "changing the lockbox code updates the upcoming job's brief" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a property with an upcoming job and lockbox code \"4821\"", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Jordan Lee")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{
            service_address: "45 Elm St",
            lockbox_code: "4821"
          })

        schedule_job(context.conn, property_path, next_week())

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :property_path, property_path)}
      end

      when_ "the owner changes the property's lockbox code to \"9077\"", context do
        "/properties/" <> property_id = context.property_path
        {:ok, edit_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/properties/#{property_id}/edit")

        {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: _path}}} =
          edit_live
          |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{lockbox_code: "9077"})
          |> render_submit()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the upcoming job's brief shows lockbox code \"9077\"", context do
        {:ok, _schedule_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert html =~ "45 Elm St"
        assert html =~ "9077"
        refute html =~ "4821"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)

    "/properties/" <> property_id = property_path

    )
    |> render_submit()

    :ok
  end

  defp next_week do
    Date.utc_today() |> Date.add(7) |> Date.to_iso8601()
  end

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp schedule_job(conn, property_path, scheduled_date) do
    "/properties/" <> property_id = property_path

    {:ok, schedule_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule")

    schedule_live
    |> element("[data-test='new-job-button']")
    |> render_click()

    schedule_live
    |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
      job: %{property_id: property_id, scheduled_date: scheduled_date}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    :ok
  end

  defp next_week do
    Date.utc_today() |> Date.add(7) |> Date.to_iso8601()
  end
end

## Phoenix 1.8 Form Component Pattern

**Structure**: Create a single LiveView module handling both `:new` and `:edit` actions with these required elements:

1. **Module Setup**
   ```elixir
   defmodule AppWeb.ResourceLive.Form do
     use AppWeb, :live_view
     alias App.Context
     alias App.Context.Schema
   ```

2. **Required Functions**
   - `render/1` - Form template with `phx-change="validate"` and `phx-submit="save"`
   - `mount/3` - Extract `return_to` param and call `apply_action/3`
   - `apply_action/3` - Pattern match on `:new`/`:edit`, set page title, schema, and form
   - `handle_event/3` - Handle "validate" and "save" events
   - `save_resource/3` - Pattern match on action, call context create/update functions

3. **Key Patterns**
   - Use `to_form(changeset)` for form assignment
   - Handle validation with `action: :validate` on changeset errors
   - Navigate on success with `push_navigate/2`
   - Support `return_to` parameter for flexible navigation
   - Use consistent flash messages: "Resource created/updated successfully"

4. **Template Requirements**
   - Wrap in layout component with flash and current_scope
   - Include header with dynamic page title
   - Form with proper field inputs and submit/cancel buttons
   - Cancel button navigates to computed return path

This pattern ensures consistent CRUD form behavior across your Phoenix 1.8 application.

# Phoenix Live Context Design Rules

## Naming Convention
- Use `AppWeb.{Feature}Live` as the namespace (e.g., `MyAppWeb.UserLive`)
- Child LiveViews use action suffixes: `UserLive.Index`, `UserLive.Show`, `UserLive.Edit`
- Child LiveComponents use descriptive names: `UserLive.FormComponent`, `UserLive.FilterComponent`

## Structure
- Each child LiveView corresponds to a unique route
- LiveComponents are shared across views in this context
- The live context itself has no code file — it is a spec-only grouping

## Scope
- Focus on a single feature area (users, accounts, orders)
- Keep the number of children manageable (typically 2-5 views + 0-3 shared components)
- Dependencies should point to domain contexts, not other live contexts

# Phoenix LiveComponent Design Rules

## Design System

Before building any UI, read `.code_my_spec/design/design_system.html` for the project's design system. Use the DaisyUI component classes and theme tokens defined there. Do not invent custom colors or component patterns that deviate from the design system.

## Assigns
- Always include `:id` assign (required by LiveComponent)
- Document all assigns in a table: Assign, Type, Required, Description
- Use typed assigns (`User.t()`, `Changeset.t()`) for clarity

## Events
- Use `phx-target={@myself}` to scope events to this component
- Communicate with parent views via `send(self(), {:event_name, data})`
- Keep event handling local — don't reach into parent assigns

## File Structure
- Place in `lib/my_app_web/live/{context}_live/` alongside sibling views
- Name files by purpose: `form_component.ex`, `filter_component.ex`

## Required Spec Sections

1. **Assigns** - Table of all assigns with types and required flag
2. **Design** - Layout structure, DaisyUI components, responsive behavior
3. **Events** (optional) - handle_event callbacks with phx-target={@myself}
4. **Dependencies** (optional) - Domain contexts this component calls

## Style Guidelines

- **Be concise** - Each section should be brief but complete
- **Use bullets** - Structure information as bullet points
- **Include context calls** - Show exactly which context functions are used
- **Show code examples** - Provide HEEx usage examples for components
- **Focus on behavior** - Describe what happens, not how it's implemented
- **Consider security** - Always include permission and authorization concerns
- **Plan for real-time** - Consider PubSub integration for live updates

Before building any UI, read `.code_my_spec/design/design_system.html` for the project's design system. Use the DaisyUI component classes and theme tokens defined there. Do not invent custom colors or component patterns that deviate from the design system.

## Guidelines

Keep liveviews small and focused.
Each liveview should correspond to a path. No modifying the UI implicitly without a path change.

## LiveView Design Template

### File Structure
- Place in `docs/design/my_app_web/{context}_live/`
- Name files by function: `index.md`, `show.md`, `form.md`

### Required Sections

1. **Purpose** - Single sentence/short paragraph describing what this LiveView does
2. **Route** - The URL pattern that renders this LiveView
3. **Context Access** - List the context functions this LiveView calls
4. **LiveView Structure** - Three subsections:
   - **Mount** - What happens when LiveView initializes
   - **Events** - User interactions and their handlers
   - **Template** - UI structure and components used
5. **Data Flow** - Numbered steps of the user journey
6. **Security** - Permission checks and authorization rules
7. **Real-time Updates** - PubSub subscriptions and live updates (if applicable)

## Style Guidelines

- **Be concise** - Each section should be brief but complete
- **Use bullets** - Structure information as bullet points
- **Include context calls** - Show exactly which context functions are used
- **Show code examples** - Provide HEEx usage examples for components
- **Focus on behavior** - Describe what happens, not how it's implemented
- **Consider security** - Always include permission and authorization concerns
- **Plan for real-time** - Consider PubSub integration for live updates

# Audit Trail — project-local append-only audit table

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Story 840: owners want to see who changed what and when (a direct MaidCentral user wish), including attributing automated recurring-job generation to the system. Entries must be immutable (criterion 7198) and filterable.

## Options Considered

- **Project-local `audit_entries` table + `Audit.Recorder`** — explicit, scoped to the events that matter, easy to attribute system actors.
- **paper_trail / ex_audit** — generic row-versioning; captures noise, awkward system-actor attribution, and both are lightly maintained.
- **Postgres triggers** — invisible to application code and hard to attribute to the acting user.

## Decision

Write a project-local `CleanerCrm.Audit` context: an append-only `audit_entries` table (actor_id nullable + `system` flag, action, subject type/id, old/new value maps as JSONB, company-scoped) with a `Recorder` API called explicitly from mutating context functions. No update/delete functions are exposed; a DB rule/constraint blocks UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth.

## Consequences

- Explicit call sites mean a mutation can forget to record; Credo local check or code review must watch for this in mutating context functions.
- JSONB old/new maps keep the schema stable as audited entities evolve.
- Retention/archival policy deferred until data volume warrants it.

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.AccountLive.Form do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account

  @impl true
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <Layouts.app flash={@flash} current_scope={@current_scope}>
      <.header>
        {@page_title}
        <:subtitle>Use this form to manage account records in your database.</:subtitle>
      </.header>

      <.form for={@form} id="account-form" phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save">
        <.input field={@form[:name]} type="text" label="Name" />
        <.input field={@form[:slug]} type="text" label="Slug" />
        <footer>
          <.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Account</.button>
          <.button navigate={return_path(@current_scope, @return_to, @account)}>Cancel</.button>
        </footer>
      </.form>
    </Layouts.app>
    """
  end

  @impl true
  def mount(params, _session, socket) do
    {:ok,
     socket
     |> assign(:return_to, return_to(params["return_to"]))
     |> apply_action(socket.assigns.live_action, params)}
  end

  defp return_to("show"), do: "show"
  defp return_to(_), do: "index"

  defp apply_action(socket, :edit, %{"id" => id}) do
    account = Accounts.get_account!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id)

    socket
    |> assign(:page_title, "Edit Account")
    |> assign(:account, account)
    |> assign(:form, to_form(Accounts.change_account(socket.assigns.current_scope, account)))
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :new, _params) do
    account = %Account{}

    socket
    |> assign(:page_title, "New Account")
    |> assign(:account, account)
    |> assign(:form, to_form(Account.create_changeset(%{})))
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_event("validate", %{"account" => account_params}, socket) do
    changeset =
      case socket.assigns.live_action do
        :edit ->
          Accounts.change_account(
            socket.assigns.current_scope,
            socket.assigns.account,
            account_params
          )

        :new ->
          Account.create_changeset(account_params)
      end

    {:noreply, assign(socket, form: to_form(changeset, action: :validate))}
  end

  def handle_event("save", %{"account" => account_params}, socket) do
    save_account(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, account_params)
  end

  defp save_account(socket, :edit, account_params) do
    case Accounts.update_account(
           socket.assigns.current_scope,
           socket.assigns.account,
           account_params
         ) do
      {:ok, account} ->
        {:noreply,
         socket
         |> put_flash(:info, "Account updated successfully")
         |> push_navigate(
           to: return_path(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.return_to, account)
         )}

      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} ->
        {:noreply, assign(socket, form: to_form(changeset))}
    end
  end

  defp save_account(socket, :new, account_params) do
    case Accounts.create_account(socket.assigns.current_scope, account_params) do
      {:ok, account} ->
        {:noreply,
         socket
         |> put_flash(:info, "Account created successfully")
         |> push_navigate(
           to: return_path(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.return_to, account)
         )}

      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} ->
        {:noreply, assign(socket, form: to_form(changeset))}
    end
  end

  defp return_path(_scope, "index", _account), do: ~p"/accounts"
  defp return_path(_scope, "show", account), do: ~p"/accounts/#{account}"
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t(),
          slug: String.t() | nil,
          members: [CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          users: [CleanerCrm.Users.User.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    has_many :members, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member, on_delete: :delete_all
    has_many :users, through: [:members, :user]

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(account, attrs) do
    account
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :slug])
    |> validate_required([:name])
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 100)
    |> validate_slug()
    |> unique_constraint(:slug)
  end

  def create_changeset(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> changeset(attrs)
    |> maybe_generate_slug()
  end

  defp validate_slug(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z0-9-]+$/,
      message: "must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    )
    |> validate_length(:slug, min: 3, max: 50)
    |> validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs, message: "is reserved and cannot be used")
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z]/, message: "must start with a letter")
  end

  defp maybe_generate_slug(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :slug) do
      nil ->
        name = get_field(changeset, :name)
        if name, do: put_change(changeset, :slug, generate_slug(name)), else: changeset

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_slug(name) do
    name
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
    |> String.replace(~r/-+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

  def list_account_members(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.list_account_members(account_id)
  end

  def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:created, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:deleted, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:updated, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.get_user_role(user_id, account_id)
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Invitations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  def subscribe_invitations(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations")
  end

  defp broadcast_invitation(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations", message)
  end

  def invite_user(scope, account_id, email, role)
      when is_binary(email) and role in [:owner, :admin, :member] and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         :ok <- validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id),
         {:ok, invitation} <- create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role),
         :ok <- send_invitation_email(invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:created, invitation})
      {:ok, invitation}
    end
  end

  def accept_invitation(token, user_attrs) when is_binary(token) and is_map(user_attrs) do
    with {:ok, invitation} <- get_valid_invitation(token),
         {:ok, user} <- resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs),
         {:ok, member} <- accept_user_to_account(user, invitation),
         {:ok, _updated} <- InvitationRepository.accept(%Scope{}, invitation) do
      {:ok, {user, member}}
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account_id) do
      InvitationRepository.list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id)
    else
      []
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(_scope, nil), do: []

  def get_invitation_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token)
  end

  def cancel_invitation(scope, account_id, invitation_id)
      when is_integer(invitation_id) and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         invitation when not is_nil(invitation) <-
           InvitationRepository.get_invitation(scope, invitation_id),
         {:ok, cancelled} <- InvitationRepository.cancel(scope, invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:updated, cancelled})
      {:ok, cancelled}
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      error -> error
    end
  end

  def cleanup_expired_invitations do
    InvitationRepository.cleanup_expired_invitations(30)
    :ok
  end

  defp validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:manage_members, scope, account_id),
      do: :ok,
      else: {:error, :not_authorized}
  end

  defp validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id) do
    case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
      nil ->
        :ok

      user ->
        if MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(user.id, account_id),
          do: {:error, :user_already_member},
          else: :ok
    end
  end

  defp create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role) do
    attrs = %{
      email: email,
      role: role,
      account_id: account_id,
      invited_by_user_id: scope.user.id
    }

    InvitationRepository.create_invitation(scope, attrs)
  end

  defp send_invitation_email(invitation) do
    url = CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/invitations/accept/#{invitation.token}"

    case InvitationNotifier.deliver_invitation_email(invitation, url) do
      {:ok, _} -> :ok
      {:error, _} -> {:error, :email_delivery_failed}
    end
  end

  defp get_valid_invitation(token) do
    case InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :invalid_token}

      invitation ->
        cond do
          invitation.status != :pending -> {:error, :invalid_token}
          DateTime.compare(DateTime.utc_now(), invitation.expires_at) != :lt -> {:error, :expired_token}
          true -> {:ok, invitation}
        end
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, %{email: provided_email} = user_attrs) do
    if provided_email == invitation.email do
      case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
        nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs)
        existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
      end
    else
      {:error, :email_mismatch}
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs) do
    user_attrs_with_email = Map.put(user_attrs, :email, invitation.email)

    case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
      nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs_with_email)
      existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
    end
  end

  defp accept_user_to_account(user, invitation) do
    inviter = Users.get_user!(invitation.invited_by_user_id)
    inviter_scope = %Scope{user: inviter, active_account_id: invitation.account_id}
    add_user_to_account(inviter_scope, user.id, invitation.account_id, invitation.role)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put

    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index

      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,

      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end
end

  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions

defmodule CleanerCrm.Authorization do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def authorize(action, %Scope{} = scope, resource) do
    case {action, resource} do
      {:read_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)

      {:manage_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:manage_members, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:delete_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role == :owner

      _ ->
        false
    end
  end

  def authorize!(action, scope, resource) do
    unless authorize(action, scope, resource) do
      raise "Unauthorized: #{action} on #{inspect(resource)}"
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users do
  @moduledoc """
  The Users context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{User, UserToken, UserNotifier}

  ## Database getters

  @doc """
  Gets a user by email.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user_by_email("foo@example.com")
      %User{}

      iex> get_user_by_email("unknown@example.com")
      nil

  """
  def get_user_by_email(email) when is_binary(email) do
    Repo.get_by(User, email: email)
  end

  @doc """
  Gets a user by email and password.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user_by_email_and_password("foo@example.com", "correct_password")
      %User{}

      iex> get_user_by_email_and_password("foo@example.com", "invalid_password")
      nil

  """
  def get_user_by_email_and_password(email, password)
      when is_binary(email) and is_binary(password) do
    user = Repo.get_by(User, email: email)
    if User.valid_password?(user, password), do: user
  end

  @doc """
  Gets a single user.

  Raises `Ecto.NoResultsError` if the User does not exist.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user!(123)
      %User{}

      iex> get_user!(456)
      ** (Ecto.NoResultsError)

  """

defmodule CleanerCrm.Integrations.Integration do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Encrypted.Binary
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: integer() | nil,
          provider: atom() | nil,
          access_token: binary() | nil,
          refresh_token: binary() | nil,
          expires_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          granted_scopes: [String.t()] | nil,
          provider_metadata: map() | nil,
          user_id: integer() | nil,
          user: User.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @providers Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :integration_providers, [:github])

  schema "integrations" do
    field :provider, Ecto.Enum, values: @providers
    field :access_token, Binary
    field :refresh_token, Binary
    field :expires_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :granted_scopes, {:array, :string}, default: []
    field :provider_metadata, :map, default: %{}

    belongs_to :user, User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(integration, attrs) do
    integration
    |> cast(attrs, [:user_id, :provider, :access_token, :refresh_token, :expires_at, :granted_scopes, :provider_metadata])
    |> validate_required([:user_id, :provider, :access_token, :expires_at])
    |> assoc_constraint(:user)
    |> unique_constraint([:user_id, :provider], name: :integrations_user_id_provider_index)
  end

  def expired?(%__MODULE__{expires_at: expires_at}) do
    now = DateTime.utc_now()
    DateTime.compare(now, expires_at) != :lt
  end

  def has_refresh_token?(%__MODULE__{refresh_token: nil}), do: false
  def has_refresh_token?(%__MODULE__{refresh_token: ""}), do: false
  def has_refresh_token?(%__MODULE__{refresh_token: _token}), do: true
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  This module defines the test case to be used by
4	  tests that require setting up a connection.
5	
6	  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
7	  import other functionality to make it easier
8	  to build common data structures and query the data layer.
9	
10	  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
11	  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
12	  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
13	  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
14	  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
15	  this option is not recommended for other databases.
16	  """
17	
18	  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate
19	
20	  using do
21	    quote do
22	      # The default endpoint for testing
23	      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint
24	
25	      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes
26	
27	      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
28	      import Plug.Conn
29	      import Phoenix.ConnTest
30	      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
31	    end
32	  end
33	
34	  setup tags do
35	    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
36	    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
37	  end
38	
39	  @doc """
40	  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.
41	
42	      setup :register_and_log_in_user
43	
44	  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
45	  test context.
46	  """
47	  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
48	    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
49	    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)
50	
51	    opts =
52	      context
53	      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
54	      |> Enum.into([])
55	
56	    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
57	  end
58	
59	  @doc """
60	  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.
61	
62	  It returns an updated `conn`.
63	  """
64	  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
65	    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
66	
67	    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])
68	
69	    conn
70	    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
71	    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
72	  end
73	
74	  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(_token, nil), do: nil
75	
76	  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
77	    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
78	  end
79	end

  tests that require setting up a connection.

  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
  import other functionality to make it easier
  to build common data structures and query the data layer.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      # The default endpoint for testing
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end

  @doc """
  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.

      setup :register_and_log_in_user

  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
  test context.
  """
  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

    opts =
      context
      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
      |> Enum.into([])

    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.

  It returns an updated `conn`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)

    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])

    conn
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
  end

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.DataCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the setup for tests requiring
  access to the application's data layer.

  You may define functions here to be used as helpers in
  your tests.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      alias CleanerCrm.Repo

      import Ecto
      import Ecto.Changeset
      import Ecto.Query
      import CleanerCrmTest.DataCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    :ok
  end

  @doc """
  Sets up the sandbox based on the test tags.
  """
  def setup_sandbox(tags) do
    pid = Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.start_owner!(CleanerCrm.Repo, shared: not tags[:async])
    on_exit(fn -> Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.stop_owner(pid) end)
  end

  @doc """
  A helper that transforms changeset errors into a map of messages.

      assert {:error, changeset} = Accounts.create_user(%{password: "short"})
      assert "password is too short" in errors_on(changeset).password
      assert %{password: ["password is too short"]} = errors_on(changeset)

  """
  def errors_on(changeset) do
    Ecto.Changeset.traverse_errors(changeset, fn {message, opts} ->
      Regex.replace(~r"%{(\w+)}", message, fn _, key ->
        opts |> Keyword.get(String.to_existing_atom(key), key) |> to_string()
      end)
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines test helpers for creating
  entities via the `CleanerCrm.Users` context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def unique_user_email, do: "user#{System.unique_integer()}@example.com"
  def valid_user_password, do: "hello world!"

  def valid_user_attributes(attrs \\ %{}) do
    Enum.into(attrs, %{
      email: unique_user_email()
    })
  end

  def unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, user} =
      attrs
      |> valid_user_attributes()
      |> Users.register_user()

    user
  end

  def user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs)

    token =
      extract_user_token(fn url ->
        Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, url)
      end)

    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

    user
  end

  def user_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    user_scope_fixture(user)
  end

  def user_scope_fixture(user) do
    Scope.for_user(user)
  end

  def set_password(user) do
    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

  def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

  def override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) when is_binary(token) do
    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(t in Users.UserToken,
        where: t.token == ^token
      ),
      set: [authenticated_at: authenticated_at]
    )
  end

  def generate_user_magic_link_token(user) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = Users.UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    CleanerCrm.Repo.insert!(user_token)
    {encoded_token, user_token.token}
  end

  def offset_user_token(token, amount_to_add, unit) do
    dt = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(:second), amount_to_add, unit)

    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(ut in Users.UserToken, where: ut.token == ^token),
      set: [inserted_at: dt, authenticated_at: dt]
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserLive.LoginTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  describe "login page" do
    test "renders login page", %{conn: conn} do
      {:ok, _lv, html} = live(conn, ~p"/users/log-in")

      assert html =~ "Log in"
      assert html =~ "Sign up"
      assert html =~ "Log in with email"
    end
  end

  describe "user login - magic link" do
    test "sends magic link email when user exists", %{conn: conn} do
      user = user_fixture()

      {:ok, lv, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        form(lv, "#login_form_magic", user: %{email: user.email})
        |> render_submit()
        |> follow_redirect(conn, ~p"/users/log-in")

      assert html =~ "If your email is in our system"

      assert CleanerCrm.Repo.get_by!(CleanerCrm.Users.UserToken, user_id: user.id).context ==
               "login"
    end

    test "does not disclose if user is registered", %{conn: conn} do
      {:ok, lv, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        form(lv, "#login_form_magic", user: %{email: "idonotexist@example.com"})
        |> render_submit()
        |> follow_redirect(conn, ~p"/users/log-in")

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry do
  @moduledoc """
  An immutable record of actor, action, subject, and old/new values.

  Append-only: no update or delete function is exposed anywhere in the
  codebase, and the `audit_entries` table itself has DB rules blocking
  UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth (see the migration that created it).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          actor_id: integer() | nil,
          system: boolean(),
          action: String.t() | nil,
          subject_type: String.t() | nil,
          subject_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          old_value: map(),
          new_value: map(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "audit_entries" do
    field :system, :boolean, default: false
    field :action, :string
    field :subject_type, :string
    field :subject_id, Ecto.UUID
    field :old_value, :map, default: %{}
    field :new_value, :map, default: %{}

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :actor, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry do
  @moduledoc """
  An immutable record of actor, action, subject, and old/new values.

  Append-only: no update or delete function is exposed anywhere in the
  codebase, and the `audit_entries` table itself has DB rules blocking
  UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth (see the migration that created it).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          actor_id: integer() | nil,
          system: boolean(),
          action: String.t() | nil,
          subject_type: String.t() | nil,
          subject_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          old_value: map(),
          new_value: map(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "audit_entries" do
    field :system, :boolean, default: false
    field :action, :string
    field :subject_type, :string
    field :subject_id, Ecto.UUID
    field :old_value, :map, default: %{}
    field :new_value, :map, default: %{}

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :actor, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
  end

  def changeset(entry, attrs) do
    entry
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :account_id,
      :actor_id,
      :system,
      :action,
      :subject_type,
      :subject_id,
      :old_value,
      :new_value
    ])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :action, :subject_type, :subject_id])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  ## Properties

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Property{} = property, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.PropertyFormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create/edit a property with its access details (entry method, lockbox/alarm codes, parking and pet notes, emergency contact). Every property belongs to exactly one client. When the host supplies `client`, the client is fixed (e.g. adding a property from a client's own page) and no picker is shown. When `client` is `nil`, the form renders a client picker and requires a selection. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |-----------------|-------------------------|----------|----------------------------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :edit` | yes | which mode the form is in | | property | `Property.t()` | yes | `%Property{}` (blank for `:new`, loaded for `:edit`) | | client | `Client.t() \\| nil` | yes | preselected client, or `nil` to show the picker | On successful save, sends `{__MODULE__, {:saved, property}}` to the parent LiveView, which decides where to navigate next. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Clients` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Clients alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header> {form_title(@action)} <:subtitle>Properties carry the access details every job brief inherits. <.form for={@form} id="property-form" data-test="property-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" >

<.icon name="hero-exclamation-circle" class="size-5" />{msg}

<.icon name="hero-exclamation-circle" class="size-5" />{msg}

<.input field={@form[:entry_method]} type="select" label="Entry Method" prompt="Select entry method" options={[ {"Lockbox", "lockbox"}, {"Keypad / Alarm", "alarm"}, {"Hidden key", "key"}, {"Other", "other"} ]} /> <.input field={@form[:lockbox_code]} type="text" label="Lockbox Code" /> <.input field={@form[:alarm_code]} type="text" label="Alarm Code" /> <.input field={@form[:parking_notes]} type="textarea" label="Parking Notes" /> <.input field={@form[:pet_notes]} type="textarea" label="Pet Notes" /> <.input field={@form[:emergency_contact_name]} type="text" label="Emergency Contact Name" /> <.input field={@form[:emergency_contact_phone]} type="text" label="Emergency Contact Phone" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Property
""" end @impl true def update(%{property: property, client: client} = assigns, socket) do changeset = build_changeset(assigns.current_scope, property, client) clients = list_pickable_clients(assigns.current_scope, client) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:clients, clients) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset))} end defp build_changeset(scope, property, nil), do: Clients.change_property(scope, property) defp build_changeset(scope, property, %Client{} = client), do: Clients.change_property(scope, property, %{"client_id" => client.id}) defp list_pickable_clients(_scope, %Client{}), do: [] defp list_pickable_clients(scope, nil), do: Clients.list_clients(scope) @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"property" => property_params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Clients.change_property(socket.assigns.property, normalize_params(socket, property_params)) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end def handle_event("save", %{"property" => property_params}, socket) do save_property(socket, socket.assigns.action, normalize_params(socket, property_params)) end # The client is fixed by the host page, not user-editable — always # trust the assign over whatever the submitted form happens to carry. defp normalize_params(%{assigns: %{client: %Client{} = client}}, params), do: Map.put(params, "client_id", client.id) defp normalize_params(_socket, params), do: params defp save_property(socket, :new, params) do case Clients.create_property(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, property} -> notify_parent({:saved, property}) {:noreply, socket} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp save_property(socket, :edit, params) do case Clients.update_property(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.property, params) do {:ok, property} -> notify_parent({:saved, property}) {:noreply, socket} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp field_errors(field) do if Phoenix.Component.used_input?(field), do: Enum.map(field.errors, &translate_error/1), else: [] end defp form_title(:new), do: "New Property" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Property" end

  @doc """
  Translates an error message using gettext.
  """
  def translate_error({msg, opts}) do
    # When using gettext, we typically pass the strings we want
    # to translate as a static argument:
    #
    #     # Translate the number of files with plural rules
    #     dngettext("errors", "1 file", "%{count} files", count)
    #
    # However the error messages in our forms and APIs are generated
    # dynamically, so we need to translate them by calling Gettext
    # with our gettext backend as first argument. Translations are
    # available in the errors.po file (as we use the "errors" domain).
    if count = opts[:count] do
      Gettext.dngettext(CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext, "errors", msg, msg, count, opts)
    else
      Gettext.dgettext(CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext, "errors", msg, opts)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Translates the errors for a field from a keyword list of errors.
  """
  def translate_errors(errors, field) when is_list(errors) do
    for {^field, {msg, opts}} <- errors, do: translate_error({msg, opts})
  end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.PropertyFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required) so this
  # test can exercise it before the sibling ClientLive.Index/Show pages
  # exist. Forwards the component's parent notification to the test
  # process so assertions can use `assert_receive`.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       socket
       |> assign(:test_pid, session["test_pid"])
       |> assign(:current_scope, session["scope"])
       |> assign(:action, session["action"])
       |> assign(:client, session["client"])
       |> assign(:property, session["property"])}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={PropertyFormComponent}
        id="property-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        client={@client}
        property={@property}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({PropertyFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a property with no preselected client" do
    test "renders a client picker listing the account's clients" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Priya Nair"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => nil, "property" => %Property{}})

      assert html =~ "Priya Nair"
    end

    test "rejects a submission with no client selected" do
      scope = scope_fixture()

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => nil, "property" => %Property{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{service_address: "123 Oak St"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='property-form']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='client-error']", "is required")
    end

    test "creates the property once a client is selected" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Priya Nair"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => nil, "property" => %Property{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']",
        property: %{client_id: client.id, service_address: "77 Maple Ave"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = property}}
      assert property.client_id == client.id
      assert property.service_address == "77 Maple Ave"
    end
  end

  describe "creating a property under a preselected client" do
    test "does not render a client picker" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => client, "property" => %Property{}})

      refute html =~ "Select a client"
    end

    test "rejects a blank service address" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => client, "property" => %Property{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{service_address: ""})
      |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='property-form']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='service-address-error']", "is required")
    end

    test "saves the property with its access details and notifies the parent" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Devon Ashe"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => client, "property" => %Property{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']",
        property: %{
          service_address: "77 Maple Ave",
          lockbox_code: "4821",
          parking_notes: "driveway only",
          pet_notes: "dog in yard"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = property}}
      assert property.client_id == client.id
      assert property.service_address == "77 Maple Ave"
      assert property.lockbox_code == "4821"
      assert property.parking_notes == "driveway only"
      assert property.pet_notes == "dog in yard"
    end
  end

  describe "editing an existing property" do
    test "preserves untouched fields and updates only the submitted ones" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      property =
        property_fixture(scope, client, %{
          service_address: "45 Elm St",
          lockbox_code: "4821"
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :edit, "client" => client, "property" => property})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{lockbox_code: "9077"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = updated}}
      assert updated.service_address == "45 Elm St"
      assert updated.lockbox_code == "9077"
    end

    test "records an audit entry naming the changed field, without the code value" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client, %{alarm_code: "1234"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :edit, "client" => client, "property" => property})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{alarm_code: "5678"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = updated}}
      assert updated.alarm_code == "5678"

      entry = Repo.get_by!(AuditEntry, subject_id: updated.id, subject_type: "Property")
      assert entry.action == "access_details_updated"
      assert entry.actor_id == scope.user.id
      assert entry.new_value["changed_fields"] == ["alarm_code"]
      refute entry.new_value["changed_fields"] |> to_string() =~ "5678"
    end
  end
end

    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({PropertyFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a property with no preselected client" do
    test "renders a client picker listing the account's clients" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Priya Nair"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => nil, "property" => %Property{}})

      assert html =~ "Priya Nair"
    end

    test "rejects a submission with no client selected" do
      scope = scope_fixture()

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => nil, "property" => %Property{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{service_address: "123 Oak St"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='property-form']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='client-error']", "is required")
    end

    test "creates the property once a client is selected" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Priya Nair"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => nil, "property" => %Property{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']",
        property: %{client_id: client.id, service_address: "77 Maple Ave"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = property}}
      assert property.client_id == client.id
      assert property.service_address == "77 Maple Ave"
    end
  end

  describe "creating a property under a preselected client" do
    test "does not render a client picker" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => client, "property" => %Property{}})

      refute html =~ "Select a client"
    end

    test "rejects a blank service address" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => client, "property" => %Property{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{service_address: ""})
      |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='property-form']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='service-address-error']", "is required")
    end

    test "saves the property with its access details and notifies the parent" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Devon Ashe"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "client" => client, "property" => %Property{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']",
        property: %{
          service_address: "77 Maple Ave",
          lockbox_code: "4821",
          parking_notes: "driveway only",
          pet_notes: "dog in yard"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = property}}
      assert property.client_id == client.id
      assert property.service_address == "77 Maple Ave"
      assert property.lockbox_code == "4821"
      assert property.parking_notes == "driveway only"
      assert property.pet_notes == "dog in yard"
    end
  end

  describe "editing an existing property" do
    test "preserves untouched fields and updates only the submitted ones" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      property =
        property_fixture(scope, client, %{
          service_address: "45 Elm St",
          lockbox_code: "4821"
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :edit, "client" => client, "property" => property})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{lockbox_code: "9077"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = updated}}
      assert updated.service_address == "45 Elm St"
      assert updated.lockbox_code == "9077"
    end

    test "records an audit entry naming the changed field, without the code value" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client, %{alarm_code: "1234"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :edit, "client" => client, "property" => property})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{alarm_code: "5678"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = updated}}
      assert updated.alarm_code == "5678"

      entry = Repo.get_by!(AuditEntry, subject_id: updated.id, subject_type: "Property")
      assert entry.action == "access_details_updated"
      assert entry.actor_id == scope.user.id
      assert entry.new_value["changed_fields"] == ["alarm_code"]
      refute entry.new_value["changed_fields"] |> to_string() =~ "5678"
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.PropertyFormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create/edit a property with its access details (entry method, lockbox/alarm codes, parking and pet notes, emergency contact). Every property belongs to exactly one client. When the host supplies `client`, the client is fixed (e.g. adding a property from a client's own page) and no picker is shown. When `client` is `nil`, the form renders a client picker and requires a selection. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |-----------------|-------------------------|----------|----------------------------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :edit` | yes | which mode the form is in | | property | `Property.t()` | yes | `%Property{}` (blank for `:new`, loaded for `:edit`) | | client | `Client.t() \\| nil` | yes | preselected client, or `nil` to show the picker | On successful save, sends `{__MODULE__, {:saved, property}}` to the parent LiveView, which decides where to navigate next. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Clients` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Clients alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header> {form_title(@action)} <:subtitle>Properties carry the access details every job brief inherits. <.form for={@form} id="property-form" data-test="property-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" >

<.icon name="hero-exclamation-circle" class="size-5" />{msg}

<.icon name="hero-exclamation-circle" class="size-5" />{msg}

<.input field={@form[:entry_method]} type="select" label="Entry Method" prompt="Select entry method" options={[ {"Lockbox", "lockbox"}, {"Keypad / Alarm", "alarm"}, {"Hidden key", "key"}, {"Other", "other"} ]} /> <.input field={@form[:lockbox_code]} type="text" label="Lockbox Code" /> <.input field={@form[:alarm_code]} type="text" label="Alarm Code" /> <.input field={@form[:parking_notes]} type="textarea" label="Parking Notes" /> <.input field={@form[:pet_notes]} type="textarea" label="Pet Notes" /> <.input field={@form[:emergency_contact_name]} type="text" label="Emergency Contact Name" /> <.input field={@form[:emergency_contact_phone]} type="text" label="Emergency Contact Phone" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Property
""" end @impl true def update(%{property: property, client: client} = assigns, socket) do changeset = build_changeset(assigns.current_scope, property, client) clients = list_pickable_clients(assigns.current_scope, client) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:clients, clients) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset))} end defp build_changeset(scope, property, nil), do: Clients.change_property(scope, property) defp build_changeset(scope, property, %Client{} = client), do: Clients.change_property(scope, property, %{"client_id" => client.id}) defp list_pickable_clients(_scope, %Client{}), do: [] defp list_pickable_clients(scope, nil), do: Clients.list_clients(scope) @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"property" => property_params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Clients.change_property(socket.assigns.property, normalize_params(socket, property_params)) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end def handle_event("save", %{"property" => property_params}, socket) do save_property(socket, socket.assigns.action, normalize_params(socket, property_params)) end # The client is fixed by the host page, not user-editable — always # trust the assign over whatever the submitted form happens to carry. defp normalize_params(%{assigns: %{client: %Client{} = client}}, params), do: Map.put(params, "client_id", client.id) defp normalize_params(_socket, params), do: params defp save_property(socket, :new, params) do case Clients.create_property(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, property} -> notify_parent({:saved, property}) {:noreply, socket} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp save_property(socket, :edit, params) do case Clients.update_property(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.property, params) do {:ok, property} -> notify_parent({:saved, property}) {:noreply, socket} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp field_errors(field) do if Phoenix.Component.used_input?(field), do: Enum.map(field.errors, &translate_error/1), else: [] end defp form_title(:new), do: "New Property" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Property" end

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

## Examples

    mix spex
    mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
    mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
    mix spex --verbose
    mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
    mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
    mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
    mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
    mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
    mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests

content.text:
I've completed the assigned work and reported to the team lead. Summary of what happened:

**Scope discovery:** Calling `start_task` with the entity_id the team lead provided actually narrowed the assignment to just `CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.PropertyFormComponent` (the codemyspec system tracks `ClientLive.Index`, `.Show`, `.FormComponent`, and the `Clients`/`Audit` contexts as separate spec'd components with their own tasks) rather than the full ClientLive context the team lead's message described.

**What I built**, since none of the `Clients` domain existed yet:
- Migrations for `clients`, `properties`, and an append-only `audit_entries` table (with DB rules blocking UPDATE/DELETE per the audit ADR)
- `CleanerCrm.Clients.Client`/`Property` schemas and a scoped `CleanerCrm.Clients` context (list/get/create/change for clients; get/create/update/change for properties, with client-ownership validation)
- A minimal `CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder`/`AuditEntry` — `Clients.update_property` records an audit entry naming which access-code field changed (never the code value itself) when lockbox/alarm/entry-method change
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/client_live/property_form_component.ex` — the actual deliverable: create/edit a property with access details, a client picker shown only when no client is preselected, `"is required"` errors on `[data-test='client-error']`/`[data-test='service-address-error']`, and it notifies its parent via `send(self(), {__MODULE__, {:saved, property}})`
- Test fixtures (`test/support/fixtures/clients_fixtures.ex`) and a component-level test suite (8 cases) using `live_isolated`, since no host route exists yet to mount it through the router

**Verification:** `mix compile` and `mix format` are clean, `mix test` passes 119/119 with no regressions. Running `mix spex` against the story 832 directory still shows 9/9 red — every scenario fails at its first step (`~p"/clients/new"` 404s) because `ClientLive.Index`/`.Show`/`.FormComponent` and the router wiring for story 832 don't exist yet — that's the remaining blocker and belongs to sibling tasks, not this one.
